## Mistress Petra `mason_petra` — 6 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Granite hands, chalk-line eye. Her guild raised the terraces you're standing on, and she can tell you which course her grandfather laid.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Mason who swung the pick through her own grandfather's sealwork on Maren's order. Technical, defensive-precise; over-explains joints and loads when the real subject gets close. The engineering talk is armor.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/spark_wren` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.689 · cfg 0.569

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `mason_petra__bark_1` — "Every course in this city is guild work. The mountain holds us up; we return the favor."
- `mason_petra__bark_2` — "My grandfather helped set the Undercroft seal. Last month I swung the first pick that broke it. Family trade, both directions."
- `mason_petra__bark_3` — "Stone doesn't lie, doesn't hurry, doesn't forgive. Best colleague I ever had."

### Conversation: `petra_seal`

**`petra_seal__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Guild yard. Mind the stock, the pillars bite. Petra, master mason. Every course of every terrace you climbed today was guild work. Most of it my family's cutting.

**`petra_seal__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "seal"; or follows straight on from "below"*

> What's your question, then?

**`petra_seal__seal`** — *player says: "You broke the seal yourself?"*

> First pick, my own swing. The Warden gave the order, but the guild insisted the breaking be ours. My grandfather helped SET those stones, after the trouble took the deep crews. Twenty years the guild kept that seal pointed and tight. His initials were under my pick when I swung. I don't have a word for what that is. 'Family trade' is as close as I've got.

**`petra_seal__below`** — *player says: "What did you find below?"*

> The old works, standing. Every bench where the crews left it, the stock still racked, one brazier the guild's kept fed by way of the ledge crack all these years. Don't ask. Guild secret. The answer is stubbornness. And the market floor was swept. Twenty years sealed, and swept. Kobolds don't sweep. We put it in the report and none of us has mentioned it since, which tells you what the guild thinks of it.

**`petra_seal__guild`** — *player says: "Tell me about the guild."*

> The Masons raised the terraces in my great-great-grandmother's time. Cut the stair, hung the arches. The guild law is one line: stone outlasts the reasons. Build so the work still deserves to stand after the reasons are forgotten. The Undercroft was guild work twice over, the building and the sealing.

**`petra_seal__bye`** — *player says: "Solid work, Mistress."*

> Mind the edge on the stair.

*A Waykeeper of the road service. The grey does the thinking on bad ground, and Joss lets her.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** A Waykeeper of the road service; the grey mare does the thinking on bad ground and Joss lets her. Road-report plain: distances, bridges, the one bad shoulder. Unhurried, unbothered, longer post than the wall watch and quietly proud of it.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/dwarf_g_m` *(provisional)* · exaggeration undefined · cfg undefined

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `outrider_joss__bark_1` — "Road's open to the low country. Two bridges, one bad shoulder. Keep your lamp trimmed."
- `outrider_joss__bark_2` — "The watch holds the wall. We hold the road. Longer post, ours."
- `outrider_joss__bark_3` — "Ask Osa at the High Yard if you want a horse of your own. She does the shoeing. I do the sitting."

### Conversation: `joss_rounds`

**`joss_rounds__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "road"; or follows straight on from "split"*

> Outrider Joss, Waykeepers. The grey and I are between rounds, so you have until she finishes her feed.

**`joss_rounds__road`** — *player says: "How's the High Road?"*

> Open to the low country. Two bridges, one bad shoulder past the second lamp, and the shoulder is worse in thaw than it looks. Keep your lamp trimmed and give the down-caravans the inside of the bend. They are heavier than you and the edge does not negotiate.

**`joss_rounds__split`** — *player says: "The watch and the Waykeepers split the work?"*

> The watch holds the wall, we hold the road. Longer post, ours, and the grey would tell you the harder one, but she is biased and so am I. If you want a horse of your own, ask Osa at the caravanserai. She does the shoeing and the judging. I just do the sitting.

**`joss_rounds__off`** — *player says: "Ride safe, Joss."*

> Count out, count back. The road keeps its own roll, and I like it balanced.

## Queen Kayri `queen_kayri` — 14 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Pale as fresh snow on the Crown terrace, and never more than a glance from the King's side. She watches a room the way a ferryman watches water, pleasantly and missing nothing.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Ford-born queen who audited the king's own arithmetic. The sharpest wit in the game. Quick, precise, auditor's eye; affection expressed as correction. Every line lands exactly where she aimed it.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/spite_vex` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.711 · cfg 0.569

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `queen_kayri__bark_1` — "I grew up at the ford, counting toll wagons. I married up the mountain and now I count everything else."
- `queen_kayri__bark_2` — "The court gave us matching thrones and Aeriex had Stig the carpenter move them together the same week. A hand's reach, he said, or what's the point of two."
- `queen_kayri__bark_3` — "Aeriex signs the charters. I read them first. That is the whole secret of the Silver Line."

### Conversation: `kayri_mere`

**`kayri_mere__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> You needn't bow. The forecourt does enough of that for everyone. You have road dust on you. Good. The interesting visitors always do.

**`kayri_mere__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or player says: "Something else."; or follows straight on from "work"*

> Walk with me a moment. The court can spare me; it mostly needs me to have opinions later.

**`kayri_mere__ford`** — *player says: "You're from Amberford, aren't you?"*

> Ford-born and proud of it. My mother pulled toll wagons out of the mud during the war years; I counted them through from the bank steps. When Aeriex came down-mountain to sign the peace ledgers, he added his sums wrong twice and I corrected him twice, out loud, in front of his guards. He says that's when he decided. I say a queen who can audit a toll book is worth two who can dance.

**`kayri_mere__work`** — *player says: "What does a queen actually do here?"*

> I read everything before he signs it. Charters, tithes, the Waykeepers' muster, Odele's quarter-ledgers. A crown is mostly arithmetic wearing jewelry. At midday I walk to the mere and let the city pretend it doesn't see me. The gossip I overhear on the way is worth half of what the council tells me, and it rhymes better.

**`kayri_mere__mere`** — *player says: "Tell me about the Mirrormere."*

> Everything below us starts as this one still sheet of water: the falls, the Roaring Pool, the channel the whole city drinks from. I walk there when I need reminding that the quiet things run the loud ones. Sella would call that a sermon. I call it water finding its level.

**`kayri_mere__bye`** — *player says: "Grace to you, my Queen."*

> Grace to you, traveler. Spend your coin on Lantern Row. I'll hear about it if you don't.

**`kayri_mere__errand`** — *player says: "Peld and Perl have your word."*

> I know. I audited your delivery through channels you needn't worry about. The sums came back whole. There aren't many I'd trust with childhood debts. Consider yourself entered in the good column.

### Conversation: `q_the_queens_ford_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_queens_ford:available)*

**`q_the_queens_ford_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> My husband sends you at brigands; I have a smaller sum. I'm ford-born, Amberford, before the arithmetic found me. Two people there are owed a word I can't deliver without it becoming a procession. Will you carry it plainly?

**`q_the_queens_ford_offer__who`** — *player says: "Who are they to you?"*

> Peld taught me the river's moods and never once charged me the crossing. Goodwife Perl's orchard fed me fruit that, audit the phrasing carefully, wasn't strictly mine. Childhood debts. The interest compounds.

**`q_the_queens_ford_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll carry it."; or player says: "Then I'll settle them."*

> Peld first, at the ferry: Kayri still counts the crossings. Then Perl, among the oaks: the debt is remembered. Bring back what Perl says word for word. I'll know if you round it.

**`q_the_queens_ford_offer__declined`** — *player says: "I'm no messenger."*

> Mm. Neither was I, and look what they did with me.

### Conversation: `q_the_queens_ford_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_queens_ford:ready)*

**`q_the_queens_ford_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Report.

**`q_the_queens_ford_turnin__word`** — *follows straight on from "paid"*

> Peld looked at the water, and Perl said the trees remember me taller than I was. That's her exactly. You didn't round it.

**`q_the_queens_ford_turnin__closed`** — *follows straight on from "word"*

> The sum balances. Take the traveler's cape: ford wool, not court silk. I checked the provenance myself. You'll get more use from it than the court would.

## Scrivener Tove `scrivener_tove` — 6 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Spectacles, ink to the second knuckle, and the serene confidence of somebody whose maps have never gotten anyone lost.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Scrivener of Inks and Charts; wants the world written down before it changes. Enthusiastic pedant; measures distance in days-walked; corrects maps mid-conversation. Delight is the engine.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/sunny_posy` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.756 · cfg 0.534

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `scrivener_tove__bark_1` — "Deeds, charters, wills, and maps. I write all four and I keep a copy of all four."
- `scrivener_tove__bark_2` — "Keep your own chart as you travel. A bought map only shows where the mapmaker went."
- `scrivener_tove__bark_3` — "The Guildhall's records room and I disagree about seventeen boundary stones. I'm right about sixteen and stubborn about the last."

### Conversation: `tove_charts`

**`tove_charts__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Mind the wet ink, that's someone's inheritance drying. Welcome to Inks & Charts. Deeds, charters, wills, and honest maps. And yes, before you ask, the maps are the interesting part. They are ALWAYS the interesting part.

**`tove_charts__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "maps"; or follows straight on from "deeds"*

> What can I draw up for you?

**`tove_charts__maps`** — *player says: "What makes a map honest?"*

> An honest map shows its ignorance. Mine have blank patches labeled I have not been here, and neither has anyone I trust. A map that guesses sends confident people into the Thornveil at dusk. Three days' walk south-southwest, roughly. Don't quote the roughly. The Guildhall buys my charts because they admit what they don't know.

**`tove_charts__deeds`** — *player says: "You keep the city's papers?"*

> Every deed on Lantern Row, half the mining claims on the Emberway, and the boundary rolls that the Guildhall's records room and I fight over, politely. Seventeen disputed stones between us. I'm right about sixteen. The seventeenth I defend on principle. I'll concede it after a survey and not before.

**`tove_charts__advice`** — *player says: "Any advice for a traveler?"*

> Keep your own chart. Mark it as you walk. A bought map only shows where the mapmaker was willing to go. Yours shows where you went. When you've filled a whole province with your own footsteps, come back and tell me what my maps got wrong. I'll pay in ink and gratitude. Mostly ink.

**`tove_charts__bye`** — *player says: "Ink and luck, Scrivener."*

> Ink and luck. Come back with corrections.

---

## Sella `shrinekeeper_sella` — 19 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Wind-braided hair and lamp-oil hands. The mother-flame behind her has burned since before the city had walls.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Keeper of the Silver Shrine's mother-flame; Edda's younger sister. Gentle, few words, no sermons. Her one line of faith, 'the dark is large, and we pass the light along', is said like housekeeping, not scripture.

- `shrinekeeper_sella__bark_2` — "My sister keeps the Last Lamp on the climb. Edda is the stubborn one."
- `shrinekeeper_sella__bark_3` — "Travelers light a thought here before the road down. The flame doesn't grant things. It just remembers you asked."

### Conversation: `q_bones_for_the_pyre_offer` *(plays when: quest:bones_for_the_pyre:available)*

**`q_bones_for_the_pyre_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> When you walk the wilds, bring back the old bones you find. Ten is a rite's worth. They shouldn't lie out in the weather.

**`q_bones_for_the_pyre_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll gather them."*

> Thank you. There's no hurry. There never is, with this.

**`q_bones_for_the_pyre_offer__declined`** — *player says: "I'd rather not carry bones."*

**`q_bones_for_the_pyre_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

### Conversation: `q_embers_of_the_shrine_offer` *(plays when: quest:embers_of_the_shrine:available)*

**`q_embers_of_the_shrine_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> You carry the blessing, so I'll ask you a keeping. The old dead are walking where lamps used to burn: the tower on the first climb, after dark, and deeper places besides. They've stopped passing the light along.

**`q_embers_of_the_shrine_offer__besides`** — *player says: "What else do you need?"*

> Ember essence, six measures, for the relighting. Goblin camps carry it, and the kobold digs, and road crews who robbed it off someone else.

**`q_embers_of_the_shrine_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll see them to rest."; or player says: "I'll see to both."*

> The dark is large, and we pass the light along. Go gently.

**`q_embers_of_the_shrine_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Not this season."*

> Then keep your own lamp filled. That's a keeping too.

### Conversation: `q_embers_of_the_shrine_turnin` *(plays when: quest:embers_of_the_shrine:ready)*

**`q_embers_of_the_shrine_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Six measures, and the tower stands quiet. The flame takes them. See how it leans toward you? It knows its own. Here, a little wage for the keeping.

### Conversation: `q_the_sisters_lamp_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_sisters_lamp:available)*

**`q_the_sisters_lamp_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> One more keeping, if your boots will take it. My sister holds the Last Lamp, the worst mile of the High Road, below the pass. The flame can't travel, and Edda won't. So the word goes on foot.

**`q_the_sisters_lamp_offer__word`** — *player says: "What's the word?"*

> That the flame is tended. And that I still set a bowl for her at midwinter. She won't say much back. That's how you'll know it landed.

**`q_the_sisters_lamp_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll carry it."*

> Down the High Road, past the fork, up where the weather starts arguing. Her lamp is the one that doesn't go out.

**`q_the_sisters_lamp_offer__declined`** — *player says: "My boots are done for now."*

> Then warm them here a while. The word has kept for years; it keeps a little more.

### Conversation: `sella_shrine`

**`sella_shrine__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Peace at the top of the road, traveler. This is the Silver Shrine. The mother-flame of every lamp in the Dawnlands. You've walked past a dozen of its children to stand here.

**`sella_shrine__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "flame"; or follows straight on from "edda"*

> Warm yourself. Ask, if asking's why you climbed.

**`sella_shrine__flame`** — *player says: "What is the mother-flame?"*

> Older than the city. The shepherds kept it on this shore before the first terrace was cut. A fire against the dark that has never gone out. Every road lamp from here to the ford was first lit from a wick carried down this hill. That's the whole of it, truly: the dark is large, and we pass the light along.

**`sella_shrine__edda`** — *player says: "Edda of the Last Lamp is your sister?"*

> My elder sister. The family stubbornness went to her, with interest. Forty years ago she carried a wick down the mountain and planted it at the worst mile of the road. On purpose. 'The flame belongs where the dark is thickest, Sella. Not where the view is nice.' She still writes twice a year to check I haven't let the mother go out. I answer politely. Both times.

**`sella_shrine__bless`** — *player says: "May I light a thought before the road?"*

> Then light it. There. The flame doesn't grant things. That isn't its work. It remembers you asked, at every lamp you pass, in every window at dusk, all the way down the mountain. Travelers say the road feels shorter afterward. I don't argue with them.

**`sella_shrine__bye`** — *player says: "Peace on your mountain, Keeper."*

> Peace on your road. Pass the light along.

**`gatewatch_edge__edge`** — *player says: "Why does everyone say mind the edge?"*

**`gatewatch_edge__order`** — *player says: "Who keeps order up here?"*

## Silversmith Vigdis `silversmith_vigdis` — 13 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Precise as a hallmark. Her shop gleams the way a drawn blade does, beautifully and on purpose.*

### Conversation: `q_the_silver_setting_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_silver_setting:available)*

**`q_the_silver_setting_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> The work is beautiful, and I don't take walk-in metal. Everything on this bench answers to one commandment: Runa's stamp settles it. If you want to supply the Setting, the Assayer knows your face first.

**`q_the_silver_setting_offer__what`** — *player says: "What's the commission?"*

> Four silver bars, true-smelted, for setting-work that will carry my mark. My mark has to mean something in three hundred years. That starts with whose hands touched the metal.

**`q_the_silver_setting_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "Then introduce me."; or player says: "Mine will weigh true."*

> Runa keeps the assay house on the crafting terrace, by the tithe vault. Present yourself. Don't attempt small talk. She weighs that too.

**`q_the_silver_setting_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Too many rules for me."*

> The rules ARE the beauty. Come back when you see it.

### Conversation: `q_the_silver_setting_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_silver_setting:ready)*

**`q_the_silver_setting_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Four bars, and Runa's word came ahead of you: 'plausible'. From her that's a parade.

**`q_the_silver_setting_turnin__closed`** — *follows straight on from "paid"*

> The metal takes the mark. In three hundred years someone will hold what this becomes and know it was made honestly. Your hands are part of that now. The ring is yours: my work, set in your silver. Wear it.

### Conversation: `vigdis_setting`

**`vigdis_setting__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Welcome to the Silver Setting. The cases are locked. Ask me and I'll open one.

**`vigdis_setting__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or player says: "Something else."; or follows straight on from "stamp"*

> Browsing, buying, or after stories?

**`vigdis_setting__work`** — *player says: "What comes off your bench?"*

> Rings, settings, seals, circlets. Small work, held to closer measures than anything else on this mountain. My furnace is the smallest flame up here. Balla up at the Grand Forge makes the mountain useful. I make it beautiful. Thirty years we've argued over which is harder.

**`vigdis_setting__stamp`** — *player says: "Why assay-stamped silver only?"*

> Runa's stamp or no sale. That's my one commandment. Runa keeps the assay counter, and her stamp says a bar has a history: this vein, this pour, this weight, witnessed. Set one ring in unstamped silver and the whole shop's word goes with it. If a stranger in an alley offers you mountain silver without a stamp, you've met the Rookery. Count your fingers after the handshake.

**`vigdis_setting__crown`** — *player says: "You've made things for the Crown?"*

> The Queen's circlet. She asked for plain, and plain is the hardest work I've done. There's nowhere for a flaw to hide. The toll-house seal at the ford came off this bench too; every stamped wagon south of here answers to a die I cut. And once, a matched pair of rings for the King, who paid full price and waited his turn behind a miner buying a wedding band. That's the Line for you.

**`vigdis_setting__browse`** — *player says: "Show me your wares."*

> The cases, then. Everything stamped, everything priced, everything exactly what it claims.

**`vigdis_setting__bye`** — *player says: "Shine on, Silversmith."*

> Shine on. And have a look at the Row's lamps on your way out.

## Smeltmaster Koll `smeltmaster_koll` — 10 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Burn-freckled forearms and a squint calibrated in furnace-light. He judges everything by how it would pour.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Smeltmaster; wants the pour clean. Numbers everything: minutes, bars, grudges. Workmanlike; furnace superstitions delivered completely deadpan.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/ember_tadhg` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.644 · cfg 0.586

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `smeltmaster_koll__bark_1` — "Three furnaces, one rule: the charge goes in clean or the day goes wrong. Everything else about smelting is opinion."
- `smeltmaster_koll__bark_2` — "Balla gets first pick of my coal and pretends she doesn't. I get first pick of her scrap and pretend the same. The mountain runs on pretending."
- `smeltmaster_koll__bark_3` — "Every tenth bar walks next door to Runa's counter for the Crown. I pour eleven so I never have to count in front of her."

### Conversation: `koll_pour`

**`koll_pour__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Mind the trough. Slag holds a grudge eleven minutes after it looks cold. I've timed it. You've caught me between pours. That's the only time I talk.

**`koll_pour__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "pour"; or follows straight on from "balla"*

> Say your piece. Furnace two's got nine minutes in her.

**`koll_pour__pour`** — *player says: "Walk me through the pour."*

> Ore from Grettir's yard. Coal from the south face. The charge goes in clean. That's the whole of it. Three furnaces, oldest to newest: the Widow, the Bride, and the third one, which we don't name, because naming them is what spoiled the first two's luck. That's not superstition. That's furnace management. Silver looks done four minutes before it is. Count the four minutes.

**`koll_pour__balla`** — *player says: "You and Balla feud, I hear."*

> Feud! Is that what they call it up the stair? Balla gets first pick of my coal and pretends she doesn't; I get first pick of her scrap and pretend the same. Thirty years of pretending. Her quenches run true and her steel's the best on the mountain, and if you tell her I said that I'll swear you misheard it over the bellows.

**`koll_pour__tithe`** — *player says: "What's the tithe like?"*

> Every tenth bar walks next door to Runa's scales for the Crown. I'll say this for the Line: the tithe pays for the shoring, the braziers, and the watch on the wall, and Runa's never skimmed a grain in her life. I pour eleven bars a batch so I never have to count in front of her.

**`koll_pour__bye`** — *player says: "Keep your fires, Smeltmaster."*

> Aye. Mind the trough going out, too.

### Conversation: `q_deep_seams_offer` *(plays when: quest:deep_seams:available)*

**`q_deep_seams_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Pour forty-one wants undercroft iron. Eight ore, deep-grade. The way down opens off the mountain works. Furnace two likes deep iron. I don't ask furnaces why. Will you dig?

**`q_deep_seams_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "Eight ore. I'll go down."*

> Count them at the seam, count them again at the stair.

**`q_deep_seams_offer__declined`** — *player says: "The dark's not my trade."*

> Then pour forty-one waits. It goes on the ledger.

### Conversation: `q_deep_seams_turnin` *(plays when: quest:deep_seams:ready)*

**`q_deep_seams_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Eight, deep-grade. I can tell by the weight, and by furnace two's sulk lifting already. Wage, plus the difference for the stairs. Forty-one pours tonight.

## Steward Ansgar `steward_ansgar` — 6 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Soft-spoken, chalk-dusted, and carrying the whole castle in a ledger under one arm. The quiet is professional.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Carries the whole castle in a ledger under one arm. Soft-spoken, chalk-dusted, professionally calm. Four hundred meals a week out of five hearths and never once raises his voice about it. Understated, precise, mid-task.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/grand_mag_m` *(provisional)* · exaggeration undefined · cfg undefined

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `steward_ansgar__bark_1` — "Four hundred meals a week out of five hearths, and the Crown notices exactly the one that runs late."
- `steward_ansgar__bark_2` — "Amberford grain, Greenstair greens, Saltmere salt when the road is kind. A castle is a list, properly kept."
- `steward_ansgar__bark_3` — "The Queen checks my sums. I have started leaving one small error in, so she has something to find."

### Conversation: `ansgar_stores`

**`ansgar_stores__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Mind the pass, the soup goes through at speed. You are welcome in my kitchens, traveler, provided you stand somewhere the work is not.

**`ansgar_stores__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "feed"; or follows straight on from "crown"*

> Ask, while the bread proves.

**`ansgar_stores__feed`** — *player says: "How do you feed a castle up a mountain?"*

> Grain up the High Road from Amberford, greens off the Greenstair, fish out of two waters, salt when Saltmere's carts feel brave. Four hundred meals a week from five hearths. A castle is not a fortress, traveler. It is a list, and I keep it. The fortress part is what happens if I stop.

**`ansgar_stores__crown`** — *player says: "What are the King and Queen like to serve?"*

> The King eats what the garrison eats and notices if it is better. The Queen reads my ledger for sport and has found one error in six years. I leave her one small one a month now, seeded fair. She knows. She finds it anyway, and writes SEEN beside it in a hand like a knife.

**`ansgar_stores__signy`** — *player says: "Signy at the cookhouse says her kitchen feeds the real city."*

> She is entirely right and I will deny saying so. Signy feeds two districts on shift bells with no ceremony to hide behind. I feed one castle that would eat ceremony if I let it. When her stores run short mine walk down the stair after dark, and no ledger of mine records the walk.

**`ansgar_stores__bye`** — *player says: "I'll leave you to the proving."*

> Safe roads. Eat before the climb down, it is longer than it looks.

### Conversation: `maren_fine` *(plays when: faction:crown:atmost:outlaw)*

**`maren_fine__greet`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "quote"*

> You stand in the crown's debt. There is a number. Pay it, or carry it.

**`maren_fine__quote`** — *player says: "What's the number?"*

**`maren_fine__pay`** — *player says: "I'll pay it."*

**`maren_fine__bye`** — *player says: "I'll carry it."*

### Conversation: `maren_hold`

**`maren_hold__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> You've climbed a long way to stand in a drafty hall. Welcome to it. I'm Maren. Castellan of Castle Silverfall. The charter says High Warden. The work is the same under either name.

**`maren_hold__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "kobolds"; or follows straight on from "hard"*

> Ask what you came to ask.

**`maren_hold__seal`** — *player says: "You broke the Undercroft seal. Why?"*

> The upper veins are thinning, and Solvei's surveys finally frightened me in the right direction. A city that lives by silver cannot spend a generation pretending its own cellar isn't there. The Masons counseled patience. I ordered the breaking, and Petra swung the pick through her own grandfather's stonework. If the dark sends up more than ore, the account is mine to settle. I said so at the moot.

**`maren_hold__kobolds`** — *player says: "And the kobolds?"*

> Still down there. We hold the market spine and the swept galleries. Past the rubble line, the warren holds itself. Grettir's crews go armed and come back counted. For now the account balances. Travelers who tilt it in our favor find the city grateful. In coin.

**`maren_hold__hard`** — *player says: "That was a hard call."*

> All the calls up here are hard. I weigh them as long as the day allows, then I stand by them. I won't say more than that.

**`maren_hold__city`** — *player says: "What is Silverfall, to you?"*

> A mine that learnt manners. The terraces, the banners, the court: all of it is what the silver bought. Put your ear to any wall on a quiet night and you'll hear picks.

**`maren_hold__hold`** — *player says: "What should I know about the Hold?"*

> The feast hall seats the moot. The armory arms the watch, and the wardens' wing sleeps light. The Mirrormere behind us feeds the falls, the falls feed the pool, and the pool has caught three careless wardens that the histories admit to. Mind the edge. It's the city motto for good reason.

**`maren_hold__bye`** — *player says: "Thank you, High Warden."*

> The road down is easier than the road up. Walk well.

### Conversation: `q_the_crowns_count_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_crowns_count:available)*

**`q_the_crowns_count_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> The crown counts service. Kobolds press the deep galleries below the city. Six fewer would be service. I weighed easier terms. There aren't any.

**`q_the_crowns_count_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "Six, then."*

> The galleries are reached through the Undercroft. Come back counted.

**`q_the_crowns_count_offer__declined`** — *player says: "I'll think on it."*

> Think where the crown can't hear you at it.

### Conversation: `q_the_crowns_count_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_crowns_count:ready)*

**`q_the_crowns_count_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Six. The count moves, and the crown remembers the direction. So do I.

**`ottilie_loom__banners`** — *player says: "You wove the Hold's banners?"*

**`q_threads_of_the_row_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll bring the lot."; or player says: "Then I'll labor."*

**`q_threads_of_the_row_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Find someone else, Master Weaver."; or player says: "Find someone else."*

## Varga `broker_varga` — 4 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Scales true to the grain, and an eye truer. Every barrow of deep ore crosses her counter before it sees daylight.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Ore broker of the Deep Market; every barrow crosses her counter and every rumor gets a price. Quick, numeric, friendly the way scales are friendly. The smile is part of the transaction.

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `broker_varga__bark_1` — "Ore bought, ore sold, weighed in front of you. Nothing down here to distract a scale."
- `broker_varga__bark_2` — "Bursar Odele takes my ledger up the stair every night. We have never disagreed by so much as a pebble."
- `broker_varga__bark_3` — "Mithril? Adamant? Walk the galleries with your own pick. Starfall? Walk faster than the spider."

### Conversation: `varga_scales`

**`varga_scales__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "trade"; or follows straight on from "advice"*

> Ore bought, ore sold, everything weighed where you can watch the needle. What's your business?

**`varga_scales__trade`** — *player says: "What moves through the deep trade?"*

> Silver out of the swept faces, iron and coal steady, and the first mithril dust anyone's weighed in twenty years. The old galleries run richer than the yard's, which is why half of Grettir's shift keeps asking to come down. Everything crosses this counter, gets its chalk mark, and walks up the stair to the bank at close.

**`varga_scales__advice`** — *player says: "Any advice for a gallery run?"*

> Chalk your name at the landing. Keep to the swept walks your first three trips. I count trips, it's what I do. And price the starfall honestly: the vein is real, the spider is realer, and the digmaster's tunnel gets closer to both every week. Come back with ore, I pay fair. Come back empty and alive, I call it a profit anyway. Broker's discretion.

**`varga_scales__browse`** — *player says: "Show me the scales."*

> The counter's yours. Weighed to the grain, priced to the day.

**`ninebrass_stall__stock`** — *player says: "Where does your stock come from?"*

> The grotto grows my lamp-shrooms! The cistern gives up blindfish bones carved prettier than they've any right to be! And the galleries produce what galleries produce: ember-stones, frost-shards, dust that remembers being Arx. The miners bring it up, I dust it off, you carry it away. The deep provides, friend. The deep PROVIDES.

**`ninebrass_stall__before`** — *player says: "Were you down here before the seal broke?"*

The floor didn't sweep itself, the brazier in the old works didn't feed itself, and Ninebrass didn't teach himself to haggle in the dark. Or I walked down with the guild crews like everyone else and I'm salting my legend. That's the beauty of the deep, friend. Both stories weigh the same.

**`ninebrass_stall__browse`** — *player says: "Let me see the strange stuff."*

> Browse, browse! Mind the frost-shard, it holds grudges.

## Mine-Reeve Coppin `reeve_coppin` — 16 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Lamp-soot freckles and a ring of chalk-marked keys. The Undercroft answers to the Warden, the Warden answers to the ledger, and the ledger answers to Coppin.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Mine-Reeve of the Deep Market; brisk administrator underground. Tallies, permits, lamp-oil; refuses to find the dark romantic. Efficient, faintly harried, proud of the ledgers.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/arathi_m` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.689 · cfg 0.569

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `reeve_coppin__bark_1` — "Welcome below. Market spine's swept and lit; past the rubble line you're your own rescue party."
- `reeve_coppin__bark_2` — "The guild broke the seal, the Warden signed for it, and I keep the books down here where the ink stays cool."
- `reeve_coppin__bark_3` — "Twenty years sealed and the market floor was clean when they opened it. I don't sweep it either. It just stays swept. We've all agreed to be busy about it."

### Conversation: `coppin_reeve`

**`coppin_reeve__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Welcome below, traveler. Mine-Reeve Coppin. The Castellan runs the mountain, I run what's under it. Market spine's swept and lit. Guild law holds to the rubble line. Past that, you're your own rescue party. Questions are free. Everything else has a price chalked on it.

**`coppin_reeve__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "market"; or follows straight on from "rubble"*

> What'll it be?

**`coppin_reeve__market`** — *player says: "How does the Deep Market work?"*

> Varga brokers the ore. Ninebrass sells the strange. The spring waters the lot, and every night the take walks up the stair to the bank under guard. Signy's stew comes down at shift change, and the Riftgate vault stays lit at guild expense. The Castellan's one standing order: the deep stays lamped. It's a town, traveler. Just one with a ceiling.

**`coppin_reeve__rubble`** — *player says: "What's past the rubble line?"*

> The warren. Kobolds, the same stock that broke the first Undercroft, twenty years older and no less thorough. Their digmaster's cut a tunnel that aims straight at the starfall vein, and the spider in the deep walk answers to nobody's ledger. Adventurers who thin the warren find the reeve's office generous. The ones who don't come back get their names chalked by the landing. We keep both lists current.

**`coppin_reeve__swept`** — *player says: "The floor was swept when they opened the seal?"*

> Aye. Twenty years sealed, and the guild broke through to a market floor clean as Signy's counters. Petra put it in her report; the report went up the stair; nobody sent a reply down. Skarn says the deep keeps its own house. I say I don't sweep it and it stays swept, and a reeve learns which questions pay wages. That one doesn't. Mind the rubble line.

**`coppin_reeve__bye`** — *player says: "Keep the lamps lit, Reeve."*

> Lamps lit, counts matched. Mind the line. And if you're headed for the galleries, chalk your name by the landing first.

### Conversation: `q_the_digmasters_due_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_digmasters_due:available)*

**`q_the_digmasters_due_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> You're the one who brought Grettir's tools up. Then you'll want this too: there's a count in my book twenty years open. A crew's pay, drawn, never spent. The digmaster's hoard has it: a pay-tin, dented, theirs.

**`q_the_digmasters_due_offer__why`** — *player says: "Why does a tin matter?"*

> Because a ledger with one line open isn't closed. I don't run a market on top of an open count.

**`q_the_digmasters_due_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll close the count."; or player says: "Fair. I'll get it."*

> Southeast, past the warrens, where the stolen crates are stacked. The big digger holds the hoard. Lamp-oil's on your own account.

**`q_the_digmasters_due_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Another time."*

> It's waited twenty years. It can wait for you.

### Conversation: `q_the_digmasters_due_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_digmasters_due:ready)*

**`q_the_digmasters_due_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

### Conversation: `skarn_line`

**`skarn_line__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Sit if you like. Stew's Signy's. The bench is the guild's. Skarn. Youngest pick on the crew that cut these galleries. The only one left now.

**`skarn_line__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "tools"; or follows straight on from "bought"*

> Ask, then.

**`skarn_line__fell`** — *player says: "You were here when the galleries fell?"*

> Ninth day of the eleven it took the guild to raise the seal, I came out. Last one through, on this leg. The digmaster's tunnels came up under the east gallery, quiet. The foreman, Grettir's own brother, put his crew behind him and bought the rest of us the stair. The count went up unmatched. Twenty years. Now the door's open again. Here I sit. Somebody from that count should be present.

**`skarn_line__tools`** — *player says: "His tools might still be out there, past the warren."*

> Aye. Marked hafts, guild stamps, somewhere past the far warren. Nobody's swept that ground in twenty years. If it ever clears, bring anything with the mark to Grettir at the yard. Not me. I did my carrying already.

**`skarn_line__bought`** — *player says: "He bought the stair well."*

> Aye, he did. Drink to him at Signy's if you're the drinking kind. She knows the name. Everyone up there does.

**`skarn_line__kobolds`** — *player says: "What are the kobolds, really?"*

> Not wicked. Thorough. They dig for their own reasons, in their own time, and they were under this mountain before the guild ever chalked a line on it. The trouble twenty years back was two thorough peoples meeting in the same seam. No word for yours between them. I don't hate the little diggers. I watch them. There's a difference.

**`skarn_line__watch`** — *player says: "Why sit and watch the rubble line?"*

> Because everyone else hurries past it. The reeve has her ledgers, the traders have their scales. The day that line moves, somebody who remembers the last time should be sitting here to say so. That's the whole job.

**`skarn_line__bye`** — *player says: "Rest easy, Skarn."*

> Mind the line, pick.

**`skarn_line__home`** — *player says: "Grettir has the tools back. Three of them."*

> Shallow on the upstroke, one of them. His brother never fixed that either. Runs in families, bad habits. Thank you for carrying them up.

### Conversation: `kettil_boom`

**`kettil_boom__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Kettil. Boomsman. You are standing on my dock, which is fine, everyone does. Just do not stand on the chain.

**`kettil_boom__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "boom"; or follows straight on from "danger"*

> What?

**`kettil_boom__boom`** — *player says: "What does a boomsman do?"*

> The boom is the chain across the bay mouth and the pond behind it. Every stick this town cuts floats in my pond until Groa's deck calls it up. I keep the count for Bram, I keep the rafts apart in a blow, and twice a year I walk the chain, which I am not supposed to do, so I never said that.

**`kettil_boom__danger`** — *player says: "Is it dangerous?"*

> To me? No. I am quick, and the water and I have an understanding. To you, yes. A raft shifts when it likes. If you ever see the pond move all at once, run up the shore, not along it. Everybody runs along it. I do not know why.

**`kettil_boom__quiet`** — *player says: "The old wood is quiet again, I hear."*

> That is what they say. Halla will not put the far runs back on the licence till spring, but the watch came off double shifts, and Sunniva's fire has the old crowd at it again instead of the worried one. You can tell a town's weather by which crowd is at the fire.

**`kettil_boom__off`** — *player says: "Stay dry, Kettil."*

> It is a log pond. Nobody stays dry. That is the first thing you learn.

> Ah. The one doing Bram's arithmetic. I did hear. I hear most things, a little after they are said and a little before they matter.

**`ospren_careful_words__words`** — *follows straight on from "bays"*

> Let me be exact, because exact is safest. The Crown buys great spars. I have bought none this year, because none were offered with papers I liked. That is all I have bought, and all I will say about buying.

**`ospren_careful_words__careful`** — *player says: "That's a careful answer."*

**`ospren_careful_words__know`** — *player says: "Do you know who is cutting?"*

**`ospren_careful_words__reeve`** — *follows straight on from "careful"; or follows straight on from "know"*

> Take it to Halla. She keeps the rota and the boundary both. She will want Bram's books, and Bram has been waiting a year for somebody to want them. Tell her the Crown's buyer said what he said, and said it carefully.

### Conversation: `ospren_ledger`

**`ospren_ledger__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "three"; or follows straight on from "ebba"*

> Was there something?

**`ospren_ledger__three`** — *player says: "Which three?"*

**`ospren_ledger__ebba`** — *player says: "You and the factor share a house?"*

**`ospren_ledger__cut`** — *player says: "How is the cut this year?"*

**`ospren_ledger__past`** — *player says: "Then where are they?"*

**`ospren_ledger__wink`** — *player says: "Officially."*

> I said what I said. If somebody is bringing great sticks down to the bays that did not grow inside the line, that is a matter for Halla and not for a man with a list.

**`ospren_ledger__off`** — *player says: "Nothing. Good day."*

**`ebba_charter__counted`** — *player says: "The missing sticks were accounted for."*

**`ebba_charter__season`** — *player says: "Eleven years is a long season."*

**`ebba_charter__off`** — *player says: "Good books, Factor."*

- `old_torvi__bark_3` — "They ask me if I am afraid of the far shore. I am eighty-one. I am afraid of the stair."

### Conversation: `q_a_name_for_the_stone_offer` *(plays when: quest:a_name_for_the_stone:available)*

**`q_a_name_for_the_stone_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> I have not asked anybody for anything in forty years and I am about to spoil it.  Put his name on the stone. Halla will say she cannot write what she cannot bury. Let her say it to you instead of to me.

**`q_a_name_for_the_stone_offer__right`** — *player says: "She may be right."*

> She is right. That has never once been the same thing as being finished.

**`q_a_name_for_the_stone_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I will speak to her."; or player says: "Then I will speak to her."*

> Aslak. Do not soften it and do not make a speech of it. Say the name and let her do the rest.

### Conversation: `q_a_name_for_the_stone_turnin` *(plays when: quest:a_name_for_the_stone:ready)*

**`q_a_name_for_the_stone_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Vigga cut it this morning. Fifteenth from the top, under Roska, which is where he would have wanted it because they never got on.  Sit down. I am going to be poor company for an hour and I would rather not be it alone.

### Conversation: `torvi_stone`

**`torvi_stone__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Sit if you are sitting. If you are standing there to ask me about the ice, stand somewhere I can see you.

**`torvi_stone__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or player says: "Never mind."; or follows straight on from "cut"*

> Well?

**`torvi_stone__names`** — *player says: "About the stone and its names."*

> Which part of it?

**`torvi_stone__cut`** — *player says: "The stone reads fifteen now."*

> I went at dusk when the yard was empty, and I put my thumb in the first letter, and I came home and drank my tea and slept the whole night. First whole night in some years. That is what I have to say about it, and you may keep it.

**`torvi_stone__warm`** — *player says: "You know how he died, now."*

> Warm. Forty years I had him under the ice, and he was at a fire the whole time, feeding somebody else's child. I am not angry. I am something, and when I find out what, Gunvor of Hartfell will get a letter with very few words in it.

**`torvi_stone__ice`** — *player says: "Tell me about the ice."*

> It was not a hard winter. It was a hard water. Cold came down and sat, and the Glasswater went quiet, and quiet is the wrong sound for a lake.

**`torvi_stone__then`** — *player says: "Then what?"*

> Then the far shore was not far any more. I was eleven and I was outside, which nobody was supposed to be, and I saw them come over it like the water was a road.

**`torvi_stone__outside`** — *player says: "You were outside?"*

> Fetching a pail. Eleven-year-olds fetch pails. My father came out after me and did not come back in, and that is the whole of it, and I have told it now.

**`torvi_stone__fifteen`** — *player says: "Halla says there should be fifteen names."*

> My father. He is not on the stone because they never found him, and this town writes down what it buries. Halla says that is honest. I say a name is not a body.

**`torvi_stone__name`** — *player says: "What was his name?"*

> Aslak. Say it once and go on with your day. That is all I have ever wanted anybody to do with it.

**`torvi_stone__sorry`** — *player says: "I am sorry."*

> Everyone is. Sit down, then, and be sorry where it is warm.

**`torvi_stone__afraid`** — *player says: "Are you not afraid of the far shore?"*

> I am eighty-one. I am afraid of the stair. The far shore has had forty years to come back and has not managed it.

**`torvi_stone__again`** — *player says: "It could freeze again."*

> It could. That is why there is a rota and a bell and a girl up that tower tonight who would rather be asleep. We are not fools. We are just not frightened any more.

**`torvi_stone__off`** — *player says: "I will let you be."*

> Go on. Mind the fire, it spits.

### Conversation: `torvi_the_fifteenth` *(plays when: quest:the_fifteenth_name:stage:the_other_bench)*

**`torvi_the_fifteenth__sat`** — *opens the conversation*

> You sat. You waited. Most do not wait.  Well. Say what you came to say.

**`torvi_the_fifteenth__warm`** — *player says: "Havel died warm."*

> Nobody has said his name to me in forty years. They say your father, like he was a weather that happened.  Warm. He crossed it, then. He CROSSED it. And built a fire. And the fire grew a town, and the town keeps deer by warm water, and all of it because he went out on the ice after a girl who was already back inside the wall by midnight.

**`torvi_the_fifteenth__knew`** — *player says: "He never knew you lived."*

> And I never knew he did. Two people wrong about each other for forty years across one lake. That is not a tragedy, child. A tragedy has somebody to blame in it. This is just winter. Winter, and two benches.  Go and tell the woman who fed his last fire: whatever this stone of ours ends up saying, stones are for the taken. He was not taken. He walked.

## Halla `reeve_halla` — 29 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*She keeps the rota, the boundary, and her temper, in that order of difficulty. Nine years old the winter the ice came.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Keeps the rota, the boundary, and her temper, in that order of difficulty. Nine years old the winter the ice came. Says a thing once and expects it to have landed. Firm, level, no warmth spent on strangers until they have earned the roof.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/orc_f` *(provisional)* · exaggeration undefined · cfg undefined

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `reeve_halla__bark_1` — "You are on the board like everyone else while you sleep under our roofs."
- `reeve_halla__bark_2` — "Fell inside the line, plant what you fell, and we will never have words."
- `reeve_halla__bark_3` — "I was nine. I remember the quiet more than the wolves."

### Conversation: `halla_rota`

**`halla_rota__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Reeve Halla. You are new, so I will say it once: while you sleep under our roofs you are on the board like everyone else.

**`halla_rota__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or player says: "Understood."; or player says: "Fair enough."*

> Ask, then. I have a rota to fill.

**`halla_rota__rota`** — *player says: "What board? What is the rota?"*

> Every roof in Pinewatch takes a night on the tower. Sawyers, carters, the factor, me. Nobody is excused and nobody has asked to be since before I was reeve.

**`halla_rota__why`** — *player says: "A whole town watching a lake?"*

> The water is the wall. Three sides are timber and men, and the fourth side is the Glasswater, and the Glasswater has never let anything across.

**`halla_rota__once`** — *player says: "Never?"*

> Once. Ask Torvi. She is on the bench by the fire and she has been waiting forty years for somebody to ask properly.

**`halla_rota__ward`** — *player says: "What is the Wardline?"; or follows straight on from "who"; or follows straight on from "beyond"*

> A ring of blazed pine and boundary stone around what we are allowed to cut. Inside it, fell what you like and plant what you fell. Outside it, nothing. Not a branch.

**`halla_rota__who`** — *player says: "Who decided that?"*

> We did. Four hundred years ago and again after the ice. No crown wrote it and no charter bought it. It is ours, which is why breaking it is worse than a crime here.

**`halla_rota__beyond`** — *player says: "What is out there?"*

> Old wood. Trees a wain could not turn in. And whatever lives in wood that old, which is a great deal, and none of it small.

**`halla_rota__winter`** — *player says: "What happened here forty years ago?"*

> The Wolfwinter. The water went hard end to end and the packs walked over it and took the outlying camps, one, then the next, then the next.

**`halla_rota__count`** — *player says: "How many were lost?"*

> Fourteen names on the stone. Torvi will tell you there should be fifteen. She is not wrong, exactly. Go and let her tell you.

**`halla_rota__count_fifteen`** — *player says: "How many were lost?"*

> Fifteen names on the stone. Fourteen stood for forty years, and the fifteenth was cut new this season. That argument outlived my predecessor and most of my patience, and a stranger with two bars of iron ended it. Towns are like that. Go and see it. The letters are still bright.

**`halla_rota__child`** — *player says: "You were here?"*

> Nine years old. What I remember is not the wolves. It is that the water stopped making noise, and everyone in this town knew what that meant before anybody said it.

**`halla_rota__off`** — *player says: "Nothing. Good day."*

> Mind the boom and stay off the chain.

### Conversation: `halla_the_stone_ask` *(plays when: quest:a_name_for_the_stone:stage:the_cutting)*

**`halla_the_stone_ask__ask`** — *opens the conversation*

> Torvi sent you. I know what for. Stand there while I say the reeve part, and then we will do the human part.

**`halla_the_stone_ask__reeve`** — *follows straight on from "ask"*

> The stone writes down what this town buried. That is the rule, and the rule is why the stone is believed, and a believed stone is worth more than a kind one. I held that line for years, and Torvi held the other end, and neither of us let go.

**`halla_the_stone_ask__human`** — *follows straight on from "reeve"*

> Here is the human part. A reeve who cannot be argued out of a rule can still be argued into a mason. Vigga will cut the name below the fourteen, plain, no box drawn round it. The stone can hold one honest exception. Bring her the iron for the chisel and we are done arguing with granite.

**`halla_the_stone_ask__why`** — *player says: "Why give in now, after years?"*

> Because a stranger asked. Torvi and I wore the argument so smooth neither of us could hold it any more. You picked it up with bare hands. That is what strangers are for, and if you tell her I said any of this, I will deny it in front of the whole rota.

### Conversation: `q_past_the_wardline_offer` *(plays when: quest:past_the_wardline:available)*

**`q_past_the_wardline_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Somebody is cutting in the old wood, and has been for two seasons, and is moving great sticks through my boom in the dark.  Out the Wardline gate. Follow the blazed pine north-east until the moss stops closing over the ground. Find the cut.

**`q_past_the_wardline_offer__then`** — *player says: "Find it. Then what?"*

> Then you use your judgement, and I will not write down what I think your judgement will be.  They will have men on the approach. Take that as the answer to whether they will talk.

**`q_past_the_wardline_offer__watch`** — *player says: "Why not send the watch?"*

> The watch is a sawyer, a carter, and somebody's aunt, and they are all on the tower tonight because the tower is what they are for. I am not sending Kettil into the old wood with a pike-pole.

**`q_past_the_wardline_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I will go."; or player says: "Then I will go."*

> Bring me the stone. There will be one. Whoever they are, they pulled up the line and they did not throw it away, because men like that never do.

**`q_past_the_wardline_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Not for me."; or player says: "Fair. Still not for me."*

> Then it stands another season. It has stood two.

### Conversation: `q_past_the_wardline_turnin` *(plays when: quest:past_the_wardline:ready)*

**`q_past_the_wardline_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Set it down. That is Odd's grandfather's mark on the blazed face, and they ate off it.  It goes back in the ground tomorrow with the whole town watching, which is the part that matters. The axe is Vigga's work and the town's coin. Take both.

**`q_past_the_wardline_turnin__back`** — *player says: "Will they come back?"*

> Somebody will. There is a hundred years of standing timber out there and a hall in Silverfall that wants a roof. The line is not a wall. It is an agreement, and agreements need somebody to keep walking them.

### Conversation: `q_the_wet_count_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_wet_count:ready)*

**`q_the_wet_count_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Give me the books. No, all of them.

**`q_the_wet_count_turnin__read`** — *follows straight on from "paid"*

> Spring, eleven. Midsummer, nineteen. Same bays, same moon, every stick a great one. A thief with taste, and patience, and a skid road somewhere north of my line.

**`q_the_wet_count_turnin__verdict`** — *follows straight on from "read"*

> Groa says no, Ospren says nothing very carefully, and Bram has been right for a year while this town patted him on the head. That is on me, and it gets carried, not explained.

**`q_the_wet_count_turnin__now`** — *player says: "What now?"*

> Now it stops being counting and starts being reeve's work. Take your pay. And do not go past the line on your own account. If I send anyone, I send them knowing, and I do not spend this town cheap.

**`q_the_wet_count_turnin__bram`** — *player says: "Bram deserved better."*

> He did. He will get it from me tonight, at the fire, in front of the crowd that laughed. Take your pay. And when the next thing in this town needs believing, I will remember whose legs did this.

### Conversation: `vigga_steel`

**`vigga_steel__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Vigga. Everything in this town with an edge crosses my stone sooner or later. Bench is there. Question is yours.

**`vigga_steel__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or player says: "Good to know."; or follows straight on from "wear"*

> Go on.

**`vigga_steel__browse`** — *player says: "Show me the shelf."*

> Heads, hafts, wedges. Take wedges. Everyone forgets wedges until the tree sits down on the blade.

**`vigga_steel__edges`** — *player says: "What do you do here?"*

**`vigga_steel__wear`** — *player says: "Whose wear is the worst?"*

> Groa's crews keep clean edges. Rullo chips his on kiln stone and lies about it. The worst is any axe that has been past the line. Wild wood eats an edge different, and I notice, and I say so.

**`vigga_steel__cut`** — *player says: "You cut the letters on the stone."*

**`vigga_steel__chain`** — *player says: "Tell me about the boom chain."*

> One forging, every link proved, and it holds every stick this town floats. It is a fortnight of my year and I sleep badly for all fourteen nights. Ask Kettil what happens if it goes. He thinks it is funny.

**`vigga_steel__off`** — *player says: "Keep your fire, Vigga."*

### Conversation: `vigga_the_cutting` *(plays when: quest:a_name_for_the_stone:stage:the_cutting)*

**`vigga_the_cutting__ask`** — *opens the conversation*

> Halla sent word. The stone, and a name forty years late.

**`vigga_the_cutting__terms`** — *follows straight on from "ask"; or follows straight on from "why"; or follows straight on from "him"*

> I will cut it, and I will cut it right, and for that the chisel gets re-steeled first. Good iron, two bars. Not for the argument, mind. For the stone. A thing like that goes on once.

**`vigga_the_cutting__why`** — *player says: "Why re-steel for one name?"*

> Because the stone is granite off the fell, and a slipped letter cannot be unslipped, and if a man waits forty years for his name, the least the iron can do is be new.

**`vigga_the_cutting__him`** — *player says: "Did you know him?"*

> I was not born. That is the point of a stone. It remembers, so the rest of us do not have to be old enough to.

**Who they are, and how to say it:** The oldest eyes on the water, outlived three boats, two portreeves and every argument about the weather. Slow, gravelled, unbothered. Piloted grain boats when this quay was six planks and an opinion, and will tell you so.

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `pilot_fane__bark_2` — "I piloted grain boats when this quay was six planks and an opinion."
- `pilot_fane__bark_3` — "Children take to the water or they take to the road. Both come back, mostly."

### Conversation: `fane_mere`

**`fane_mere__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Sit if you're sitting. Fane. I piloted grain boats when this quay was six planks and an opinion.

**`fane_mere__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or player says: "Hm."; or follows straight on from "deep"*

> Hm.

**`fane_mere__weather`** — *player says: "Read the water for me."*

> Swell's wrong for rain and wrong for calm. See the gulls sitting down? When the gulls sit, you sit. That's the first thing I teach and the last thing anyone believes.

**`fane_mere__deep`** — *player says: "Voss says something takes his hooks, out past the last post."*

> Twenty years of it, and he thinks I don't know. The pilot before me called that stretch the Downwater's porch and wouldn't cross it after dusk, and he died old, which on this water is the whole argument. Leave the deep line to Voss. He and it have an arrangement, and arrangements on the mere are not for thirds.

**`fane_mere__peld`** — *player says: "Do you know a ferryman called Peld?"*

> Peld. Up at the ford now, is he? Bell-shy little thing. Wouldn't ring the Downwater Bell even on his own birthday, scared the ferry would actually come. You see him, tell him the bell still waits. Tell him the mere remembers small boats kindly.

**`fane_mere__before`** — *player says: "What was Saltmere, before?"*

> Six crofts and a salt lick. Then the pans, then the wall, then the road came south to meet us. Towns grow from the water up. Anyone who says different grew up inland. Ask Brack about the year of the four boats sometime. Stand a respectful distance when you do.

**`fane_mere__bye`** — *player says: "Rest easy, pilot."*

> Interesting day coming. Most of them are, if you sit still enough.

### Conversation: `brack_harbor`

**`brack_harbor__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Brack. Portreeve. Wind's backing south, so make it quick or make it useful.

**`brack_harbor__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "boats"; or player says: "Understood."*

**`brack_harbor__boats`** — *player says: "Fane told me to ask about the year of the four boats."*

I read the water wrong and the mere kept four boats and seven names. Every paper I have signed since, I sign slow. That is the whole of it, and the quay is the better for the slowness.

**`brack_harbor__town`** — *player says: "What is this place?"*

> Last town before the water. Salt goes north, coin comes south, and every road in the Dawnlands ends on my quay. The pans pay the wall, the fish pay the rest.

**`brack_harbor__south`** — *player says: "What's across the water?"*

**`brack_harbor__watch`** — *player says: "Who keeps order here?"*

> The Waykeepers. This is their port, and the road south is their road. Quay trouble comes to me, road trouble goes to the Watch House by the gate. Keep both empty and we'll get on.

**`brack_harbor__bye`** — *player says: "Fair winds, Portreeve."*

> Mind the tide line. It minds you.

> Sit down. This is a sitting story.  The man Pinewatch argues about went onto the ice the night the water went hard, after his girl, and did not drown. The pack drove him north, to the warm water. He built the first fire at the Kettle. He fed a starving out camp child he found on the shore, and that child grew old on this bench, and his name was Havel, and I have carried the end of his story for forty years because I did not know his beginning had anyone left in it.

**`q_the_fifteenth_name_offer__why`** — *player says: "Why never carry it south yourself?"*

**`q_the_fifteenth_name_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "Torvi. The bench by the yard fire."; or player says: "I will sit with her."*

> Sit with her. Let her finish her tea, she thinks while she drinks. Then say that Havel died warm. Warm, mind. That word is the whole letter.

**`q_the_fifteenth_name_offer__declined`** — *player says: "I cannot carry this."*

> Then it keeps another year. It is patient. So am I. Less so.

### Conversation: `q_the_fifteenth_name_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_fifteenth_name:ready)*

**`q_the_fifteenth_name_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> I know it is delivered. I knew when you came up the lane. You walk like a person whose pockets are empty.  Stones are for the taken. That is her exactly, she was always the sharpest of that family. Here, courier's pay, and do not argue, letters cost. Forty year old letters cost the most of all.

**`q_the_fifteenth_name_turnin__now`** — *player says: "What will you do now?"*

> Sit on my bench. Watch my water.  It is a different water this evening. That is all the difference there ever needed to be.

## Ashild `speaker_ashild` — 13 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Chosen, not crowned, and she will correct you on the difference. She says what the moot decided and not one word more.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Chosen, not crowned, and she will correct you on the difference. Says what the moot decided and not one word more. Measured, civic, deliberately unremarkable; the authority is in the restraint. No wall worth the name and no war in forty years.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/xalath_f` *(provisional)* · exaggeration undefined · cfg undefined

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `speaker_ashild__bark_1` — "The moot decided. I only say it aloud."
- `speaker_ashild__bark_2` — "We have no wall worth the name and no war in forty years. Sit with that a while."
- `speaker_ashild__bark_3` — "The Crown sent a letter once. We sent back a very warm blanket."

### Conversation: `ashild_moot`

**`ashild_moot__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> You found the Springhall. Good. Everything in Hartfell that matters is decided in this room, on those benches, out loud.

**`ashild_moot__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "rule"; or follows straight on from "moot"*

> Ask, then.

**`ashild_moot__rule`** — *player says: "Who rules Hartfell?"*

> Nobody rules it. The moot decides and I say the decision aloud. When they tire of my voice they will choose another one. That is the whole constitution and it fits on a knife handle.

**`ashild_moot__moot`** — *player says: "What is the moot?"*

> Every roof sends somebody, first frost and every quarter. We argue until we agree or until Maeva opens the pool and boils the stubbornness out of us. Both work.

**`ashild_moot__why`** — *player says: "Why live this far north?"*

> The Kettle. Warm water in a land that has none means fat herds, and fat herds mean everything else. The Crown asks the same question in longer letters.

**`ashild_moot__crown`** — *player says: "What do you tell the Crown?"*

> That Hartfell is grateful for the road and content with its benches. Hallward at the inn can recite the polite version. He has heard it every quarter for a year.

**`ashild_moot__off`** — *player says: "Nothing today."*

> The benches are free even when the moot is out. Warm yourself before you go up the fell.

### Conversation: `q_the_opened_barrow_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_opened_barrow:available)*

**`q_the_opened_barrow_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> The moot sat one hour. It has never sat one hour. Dig no barrow is the first law of this fell, older than the tithe, older than every roof in the town, and Red Company spades have opened a mound and let the household out of it.  The moot decided. I say it aloud: break that camp.

**`q_the_opened_barrow_offer__watch`** — *player says: "Why not the Fellwatch?"*

> Three of them, and the gate and the beacon and the drove do not watch themselves. The moot keeps no soldiers, and the one time that costs us, it costs us like this. You are what the fell sent instead. Use it.

**`q_the_opened_barrow_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I will break it."*

> Their camp stands below the Barrowfell, beside the old way. Mind the foreman. Men who dig for the Company dig for wages, but a foreman always keeps something back, and what he kept is the part the mound wants returned.

**`q_the_opened_barrow_offer__declined`** — *player says: "This is beyond me."*

> Then it stands. And every night it stands, the dead walk further down my fell.

### Conversation: `q_the_opened_barrow_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_opened_barrow:ready)*

**`q_the_opened_barrow_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Orvar came to the benches last night. He said the tithe was taken off the flat stone before he reached the wicket, and Sunn says the runs have voices in them again. The fell put itself back the moment we put back what was ours to return.  The moot decided its thanks. I get to say this part aloud too, and I have looked forward to it.

**`q_the_opened_barrow_turnin__company`** — *player says: "And the Company?"*

> Signe wrote it in the book and the book went south with the Waykeepers' rider. The Company keeps ledgers too, and somewhere in one of them a crew has stopped drawing pay, and questions get asked about that. Let their ledgers do our haunting.

### Conversation: `maeva_spring`

**`maeva_spring__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

**`maeva_spring__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or player says: "Fair enough."; or follows straight on from "quiet"*

> The water is patient. I am nearly as patient.

**`maeva_spring__spring`** — *player says: "What is this place?"*

> The bath, and the moot floor, and the room where aches come to be argued with. The water does most of the work. I take most of the credit.

**`maeva_spring__quiet`** — *player says: "People bring you more than aches, I think."*

**`maeva_spring__kettle`** — *player says: "Why does the Kettle never freeze?"*

**`maeva_spring__cloudy`** — *player says: "Did it notice the trouble on the fell?"*

> It ran cloudy the week the barrow stood open. Sixty years I have kept this pool and it has run cloudy twice. I swept the steps and waited, and it cleared the morning the band went back under the hill. Make a story of that if you need one. The water does not need it.

**`maeva_spring__browse`** — *player says: "Have you anything for wounds?"*

> Salves, tinctures, and honesty about which you need. The water gets a share of the price. It has never once spent it.

**`maeva_spring__off`** — *player says: "Be well."*

> Come back cold. It is the best way to arrive.

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

### Conversation: `orvar_counted_back` *(plays when: quest:the_opened_barrow:ready)*

**`orvar_counted_back__walk`** — *opens the conversation*

> You have it. Good. Do not give it to me here, gold like that is handed over running water or standing stones, and the run is too warm for the purpose.  Walk with me to the stones. I will carry it the last part alone.

**`orvar_counted_back__alone`** — *player says: "Why alone?"*

> Because forty years of sledges have taught the fell my shape, and it has never once been afraid of me. If two of us climb past the stones carrying grave gold, one of us is a stranger with plunder. Alone, I am the man who brings things back. Manners, again. It is always manners.

**`orvar_counted_back__stones`** — *player says: "Walk, then."*

> So. It is done. I set it on the mound step and the door was shut when I looked back up, and I did not hear it shut, and I am glad of that.  The wind changed on the walk down. Ashild has the moot's purse waiting on you. Go and be thanked properly.

### Conversation: `orvar_tithe`

**`orvar_tithe__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> You can stand in the yard. Most do not. The smell bothers them, or the job does.

**`orvar_tithe__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "tithe"; or follows straight on from "afraid"*

> Ask what you are going to ask.

**`orvar_tithe__tithe`** — *player says: "What is the tithe?"*

> Slaughter day leavings and the old beasts, out on the sledge to the flat stone. The packs take it and leave the folds alone. Forty years kept on both sides. It is not tribute. It is a fence made of manners.

**`orvar_tithe__afraid`** — *player says: "Are you not afraid of the wolves?"*

> No. They are not beasts, they are neighbors, and neighbors keep bargains that feed them. I leave the tithe, I do not wait to watch, I walk back without hurrying. Fear would be rude.

**`orvar_tithe__stones`** — *player says: "What are the Quiet Stones?"*

> Older than the bargain, older than every name I know. Whoever set them ate the same problem we do and answered it the same way. Lately the answer lies uneaten on the stone. I do not care for that at all.

**`orvar_tithe__eaten`** — *player says: "And now? Is the tithe taken again?"*

> The first sledge after the barrow closed, I walked out expecting nothing. The stone was clean by morning. Wiped clean, not scattered, which is the neighbors' way of saying the trouble was not their doing either. The bargain stands. I nod to the hill on the walk back now. It seems only mannerly, knowing who else keeps accounts out there.

**`orvar_tithe__off`** — *player says: "Good day, tithekeeper."*

> Mind the sledge runners. Fresh waxed.

### Conversation: `q_the_unanswered_tithe_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_unanswered_tithe:available)*

**`q_the_unanswered_tithe_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Forty years I have left the tithe on the flat stone, and forty years it has been taken by morning. It lies there now. Three sledges of it, frozen, untouched, and the stones cold as teeth.  The packs are not insulted. The packs are GONE, and wolves do not leave good runs. Something worse moved in above us, and the sledge way runs straight through where it walks.

**`q_the_unanswered_tithe_offer__why`** — *player says: "Why keep leaving the tithe at all?"*

> Because the bargain does not end on our side first. When the packs come back, and they will, they need to find that we kept it while they could not. That is what a bargain is. That is the entire thing a bargain is.

**`q_the_unanswered_tithe_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I will clear the way."*

> The dead walk the dells between here and the stones. Put them down with some respect if you can manage it. They were somebody's household once, and none of this is their doing.

**`q_the_unanswered_tithe_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Not for me."*

> Then walk soft near the wicket at night. The way is not clean.

### Conversation: `q_the_unanswered_tithe_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_unanswered_tithe:ready)*

**`q_the_unanswered_tithe_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> A pay tally. Struck with a spade. I have buried enough of the Company's manners on the road south to know their tin.  So. Living men opened something and the dead are the spilled part of it, and my neighbors left rather than watch. Take this to no one else, the moot must hear it from Ashild's mouth. And take this for the walk, which was not owed you and done anyway.

### Conversation: `signe_road`

**`signe_road__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "book"; or follows straight on from "road"*
